skill.displayName: Lingxi-MindVault - Auto Memory Extraction for OpenClaw

llm.summary: The skill mostly does what it claims (scan OpenClaw sessions and write extracted results to Feishu), but there are several inconsistencies and data-exposure risks you should understand before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name/description align with the scripts: they scan OpenClaw session files, extract memories via the OpenClaw agent and write results to Feishu (L2/L3/L4). Declared required environment variables (FEISHU_*) match the stated Feishu integration. However, the package metadata declares no required binaries while the scripts clearly require the openclaw CLI and python3 (and optionally inotify-tools/jq per README). The omission of required binaries is an inconsistency that could cause runtime failures or surprise about required capabilities.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and scripts read local OpenClaw session files and sessions.json (expected for the stated purpose). BUT the do_extract_and_write.sh builds an AI prompt by substituting environment variables (including L2_APP_TOKEN, L2_TABLE_ID, L3_DOC_ID, L4_DOC_ID) into a temporary prompt file and passes that prompt to 'openclaw agent' as plain text. This means Feishu tokens and doc/table IDs are written into /tmp/ai_prompt_* and transmitted in a prompt to the agent process. Storing credentials in temp prompt files and embedding them into prompt text increases risk of credential exposure (to logs, other processes, or agent plugins). The scripts also source workspace/.env and rely on openclaw CLI tool behavior; the instructions are not vague but grant the agent direct ability to call tools that send data externally (Feishu).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill (no package install), which is lower risk than downloading arbitrary binaries. However, the scripts assume tools (openclaw CLI, python3, possibly jq/inotify-tools) are present; the skill does not declare these required binaries in metadata. Installation instructions ask the user to copy scripts into the workspace and add cron entries — these require manual action and privilege to edit crontab, which is expected for this functionality.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The set of required environment variables (FEISHU_USER_OPEN_ID, L2_APP_TOKEN, L2_TABLE_ID, L3_DOC_ID, L4_DOC_ID) is reasonable for a Feishu-writing skill. HOWEVER, the implementation embeds these secrets directly into the AI prompt and writes them to temporary files. That is disproportionate and increases credential exposure risk. The skill does not request unrelated credentials, but it does require access to local OpenClaw session files (sensible) and will transmit session content to Feishu (expected but privacy-sensitive).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always: true and does not request elevated or platform-wide persistence. Installation instructions ask the user to copy scripts into workspace and optionally add cron entries — normal for a scheduler-based utility. The skill does not modify other skills' configs or system-wide agent settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to implement the described automatic extraction and writing to Feishu, but take care before installing:

- Expect it to read your OpenClaw session files and send their content to Feishu. Do not use this if your sessions contain sensitive personal, financial, or regulated data.
- The scripts require the openclaw CLI and python3 (and optionally jq/inotify-tools) but the metadata does not list those binaries — ensure those tools are installed and trusted before running.
- The do_extract_and_write.sh substitutes your Feishu tokens and IDs into a prompt file (/tmp/ai_prompt_*) and passes that text to openclaw agent. That means your L2_APP_TOKEN, L2_TABLE_ID, L3_DOC_ID, L4_DOC_ID can end up in temporary files, agent inputs, and potentially logs. If an attacker or other local process can read /tmp or agent logs, tokens could be exposed. Consider this a high-risk design choice.
- Mitigations: run the skill in an isolated environment, use least-privilege Feishu app tokens (scoped only to the exact tables/docs needed), rotate tokens if exposed, secure /tmp (or modify scripts to avoid writing credentials to disk), and review openclaw agent network behavior and logs. Prefer passing credentials via secure IPC or tool invocation rather than embedding them into prompt text.
- If you plan to install: review and modify scripts to avoid writing secrets to temporary files and avoid including tokens in prompt text; add explicit required-binaries metadata (openclaw, python3); and test in a non-production environment first.
